independence_declaration.statement: I am domain-reviewer, run T-DG1-REV-DOM-R12. I authored no implementation, register text or decision in the DG1 scope. The round-12 repair (rule 5 in apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts and its self-checks in architecture.test.ts, commit 792973b, task T-DG1-BE13) was written by backend-workflow-engineer. F-DG1-133 was raised by code-security-reviewer in round 11. I verify it here as another qualified non-author, as my role assignment directs. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-12 record, and none was visible to me: docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-12 did not exist during my run. I re-used my own role's round-11 harness scripts as round-12 copies, changing only the header lines, the diff range and the findings list. I grant no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 is not engineering gate DG7.

checks_run.procedure: Confirm the frozen candidate. Check HEAD, that the repository is not shallow, and the recomputed candidate ID, both in the repository and in a full disposable clone checked out at the freeze commit 987ae02. Check that HEAD differs from the freeze commit only in candidate-excluded metadata, and that the fix commit 792973b is an ancestor of the freeze commit.
checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG1; git clone . $TMPDIR/rev && git checkout 987ae02 && node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG1; git diff --stat 987ae02 HEAD; git merge-base --is-ancestor 792973b 987ae02
checks_run.environment: Linux sandbox; repository /home/user/My-owns (HEAD e77be1a) and a full disposable clone under $TMPDIR (removed afterwards)
checks_run.expected: candidate_id sha256:619d74ff…dfac (391 files) in both computations; 987ae02..HEAD limited to excluded metadata; the fix commit is an ancestor
checks_run.actual: Both computations give sha256:619d74ffa4e668933960fc14aa5d8c4c31850a2772972bceb647561be2efdfac (391 files). Neither tree is shallow. HEAD e77be1a differs from the freeze commit only by the round-12 review assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json, all of which the candidate excludes. 792973b is an ancestor of 987ae02. HEAD is not the source_commit, but the assignment names 987ae02 as the freeze commit and the candidate ID matches, so this is not a mismatch.

checks_run.procedure: Read the testkit header and the JSDoc of SAFE_NODE_BUILTINS and NAMESPACE_RESTRICTED_BUILTINS. Grep for the wording the finding called inaccurate. Check that residual (a) now describes only plain-object and third-party data flow, that rule 5 is documented, and that the cited plain-object idiom matches the real call sites.
checks_run.command: grep -n -i 'not closable statically|identity/routes.ts|access/rules.ts' apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; sed -n '/Residual limits/,/(b) F-DG1-127/p' apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; grep -n 'Object.entries' apps/api/src/modules/identity/routes.ts apps/api/src/modules/access/rules.ts
checks_run.expected: No 'not closable statically' and no identity/routes.ts or access/rules.ts citation in the testkit. Residual (a) is limited to plain-object or third-party data flow and states that no allow-listed built-in namespace reaches it. Rule 5 is documented with the forms it flags.
checks_run.actual: The grep finds no match (exit 1). Residual (a) now reads 'runtime DATA FLOW over PLAIN OBJECTS and third-party readers'. It keeps `new Map(Object.entries(request.cookies)).get(name)` as legitimate. It says 'No allow-listed built-in NAMESPACE reaches this residual any more', because node:crypto can no longer be namespace- or default-bound (rule 5), and that the former E-forms are 'a violation at the import'. The heading changed from 'not closable statically' to 'ACCEPTED by choice: this is a defence-in-depth lint over human-reviewed code'. Rule 5 is listed in the header with every flagged form, and the member audit says the enumeration route is CLOSED by rule 5. identity/routes.ts:35 (request.cookies) and access/rules.ts:55 (PERMISSIONS) are plain objects, as the new test title 'identity/routes.ts, access/rules.ts idiom' now correctly describes them. The description is accurate.

checks_run.environment: disposable clone of 987ae02; node v22.22.2 and v24.21.0

checks_run.procedure: Check independently that rule 5 neither over-reaches nor leaves the route open, using a reviewer-authored probe that calls fileViolations and moduleViolations directly. Allowed (16 cases): many and aliased named crypto imports, typeof import('node:crypto'), named and as-default re-exports of a crypto function, namespace/default/dynamic/export-star imports of fs, fs/promises, os, path, url and util, and plain-object Map/Object.entries enumeration. Flagged (15 cases): every binding form, including the string-literal name { "default" as c }, a template-literal import(`node:crypto`), import('node:crypto').then(enumerate), a bare 'crypto' namespace and a computed import(). Also: every real module has zero violations. The probe ran in the disposable clone and was removed afterwards.
checks_run.command: cp 02-rule5-scope-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom-r12-probe.test.ts; PATH=<node bin>:$PATH node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-dom-r12-probe.test.ts --reporter=verbose; rm the probe
checks_run.environment: disposable clone of 987ae02; node v22.22.2 and v24.21.0
checks_run.expected: 32/32 on both runtimes: the 16 allowed cases give 0 violations, the 15 binding cases give at least 1, and the real tree gives 0
checks_run.actual: 32/32 passed on Node v22.22.2 and on Node v24.21.0 (exit 0). Only node:crypto (and bare 'crypto') namespace/default bindings are restricted. Named imports and the namespace imports of the other allow-listed built-ins are unaffected, and all 13 modules have zero violations. Every source import of node:crypto in apps/ and packages/ is a named import (13 sites).
